THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173 (1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 16.05.2019 PASSED IN MVC NO.562/2017 BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND JMFC, HOLALKERE AND ETC.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ORDERS, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT
This appeal is preferred by the claimant challenging the judgment and award passed by Senior Civil Judge and JMFC, Holalkere (for short 'the tribunal') in MVC.No.562/2017 dated 16.05.2019.
This appeal is founded on the premise of inadequacy of compensation.
2. Though this matter is listed for orders, with consent of learned counsel on both sides, matter is taken up for final disposal.
3. Parties to the appeal shall be referred to as per their status before the tribunal.

4. Brief facts of the case is as under:
On 14.09.2015 at 10.15 a.m., when the claimant and his uncle were going towards main circle at Holalkere town by walking on the left side of the road, at that time, a bus bearing registration No.KA-16/B-3015 came with high speed in a rash and negligent manner so as to endanger human life and safety, dashed against the claimant from behind, thereby causing accident resulting in grievous injuries being sustained by the claimant, immediately after the accident, the claimant was taken to Government Hospital, Holalkere where he took initial treatment and on the basis of advice of Doctor, he was shifted to Davanagere Private Hospital and thereafter shifted to Chitradurga Private Hospital for further treatment and despite having taken treatment in three hospitals, he is still undergoing further treatment.
It is also stated by the claimant that he has expended huge amount of money for his treatment and due to the fracture suffered, as a result of the accident, his future earning capacity is diminished.
Hence, he has filed a claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation.
4.1. On service of notice, respondents appeared before the tribunal and filed their separate statement of objections denying the claim made by the claimant.

Respondent No.1 took up the plea that the claim petition is not maintainable and also stated that he is not liable to pay the compensation where as respondent No.2 denied entire claim petition inter alia contending that the accident occurred due to the fault of claimant while he was suddenly crossing the road without observing traffic rules.
Respondent No.2 has also taken the plea that the documents produced by the claimant are all fabricated and concocted and hence, it is not liable to pay any compensation.
It is also pleaded by respondent No.2 that the driver of the alleged bus had no valid licence to drive class of vehicle as on the date of occurrence of accident.
Hence, on this ground, he has sought for dismissal of claim petition.
4.2. The tribunal framed relevant issues for consideration on the basis of pleadings of the parties.

4.3. In order to substantiate the issues and to establish his case, the claimant got himself examined as PW.1 and also the Doctor as PW.2 and got marked the documents as per Exs.P1 to P19 in support of his case.

On the contrary, respondent No.2 examined its Officer as RW.1 and produced two documents as Exs.R1 and R2.
4.4.

On the basis of material evidence both oral and documentary, the tribunal has awarded compensation of Rs.1,45,133/- with interest @ 6% p.a.
5.
Being dissatisfied with the amount of compensation awarded by the tribunal, the claimant is before this Court in this appeal seeking enhancement of compensation awarded by the tribunal.

6. It is the vehement contention of learned counsel for claimant that the tribunal has grossly erred in awarding meager compensation so also has erred in not taking into consideration the material evidence both oral and documentary, thereby causing miscarriage of justice to the claimant.

It is further contended that the tribunal has erred in not awarding suitable compensation towards medical expenses based on records and has committed an error in awarding meager amount of 17,373/- which requires interference by this Court.

He has also further contended that the tribunal has committed gross error in not awarding proper future loss of income due to disability suffered by the claimant and has not applied its mind in assessing the proper income of the claimant based on avocation and evidence on record.
It is also contended by learned counsel that the tribunal has erred in not calculating the correct disability for assessing the loss of future earning capacity.
On the basis of these submissions, he seeks to allow the appeal and consequently, seeks enhancement of compensation.

7. Per contra, learned counsel for respondent-Insurer vehemently contends that the judgment and award passed by the tribunal is in accordance with material evidence both oral and documentary and same does not call for any interference by this Court for the reason that the tribunal has considered the age and avocation and no material document produced with regard to proof of income and accordingly, notional income has been adopted by the tribunal, which does not call for interference by this Court.
He also contends that the tribunal has awarded just and reasonable compensation under all other heads.
Hence, no interference is called for in the present case as the appeal is devoid of merit and same deserved to be dismissed.
On the basis of these submissions, he seeks for dismissal of the appeal and to affirm the judgment and award passed by the tribunal.

sentences.text:
Having heard the submissions of learned counsel for appellant-claimant and learned counsel for respondent- Insurer, the points that would arise for consideration are:-
"(i) Whether the tribunal has awarded meager compensation and has committed an error in not considering the material evidence on record?
(ii) Whether there is any need to enhance the compensation awarded by the tribunal?"

9. On careful perusal of entire material evidence placed before the Court, it is seen that accident occurred on 14.09.2015 at about 10.15 a.m. when the claimant and his uncle who were walking by the side of road, a bus bearing registration No.KA-16/B-3015 drove the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the claimant from behind, due to which, the claimant sustained injuries.
In order to establish this fact, the claimant has produced Exs.P1 to P8 which are FIR, complaint, spot mahazar, seizure mahazar, rough sketch, IMV report and charge sheet.

Based on these Police records, it is seen that the jurisdictional Police after conducting investigation and enquiry had laid the charge sheet as against the driver of the offending bus, which is not seriously disputed.

The charge sheet filed by the Police is also not in challenge so also no material evidence has been placed before the Court to dispute the charge sheet and the criminal case registered against the driver of the bus.
Hence, it can be inferred that in view of criminal case having been filed against the driver of the bus, the liability is rightly attributed against the driver of the offending bus.

10. Coming to aspect of income, avocation and age of the claimant, though it is stated by the claimant that he was B.Sc. Graduate with first class, but he has not produced any material evidence to prove his income.

11. In view of there being no proof of income, the tribunal has assessed the income at Rs.6,000/-
p.m.
Admittedly, in the present case on hand, no material documents have been placed by the claimant to prove his income.

However, in a case where there is no proof of income, the tribunal and this Court are left with no other option but to rely on certain guess work and in order to do the same,
the standard procedure is prescribed by the Legal Services Authority with regard to the notional income for the relevant year of accident.
The accident having occurred in the year 2015, the notional income is prescribed as Rs.9,000/-.
Accordingly, I deem it appropriate to assess the notional income of the claimant in present case as Rs.9,000/- as against Rs.6,000/- assessed by the tribunal.
12. With regard to the age of claimant, the tribunal has assessed the age of the claimant as 20 years.

Hence, the age of the claimant to be taken as 20 years and in view of the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (Smt) and others vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in (2009) 6 Supreme Court Cases 121, the appropriate multiplier would be '18',
which is rightly taken by the tribunal and the same does not call for interference.

sentences.text: 13. The claimant has got examined the Doctor as PW.2 namely, Dr.Ambarish who has issued Ex.P15 being the disability certificate.

It is also stated by PW.2 that the claimant has sustained permanent physical disability to an extent of 20% to the right lower limb and 8% to his spine whereas on careful Devaraj K S vs Marulasiddeshwara R J on 31 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107752679/

sentences.text: perusal of Ex.P13, it is evident that there is a prominence of ligamentum flavum at L-5 S-1 level and other things are normal.
Therefore, considering the disability opined by the Doctor to an extent of 20%, the tribunal has assessed the disability to an extent of 6%.
However, the tribunal has failed to take into consideration the disability of 8% opined by the Doctor with regard to spine.

Though there may not be a major disability of spine,
- 10 - but the opinion of the Doctor has to be appreciated.
The total disability with regard to right lower limb and spine will have to taken together for assessment.

Therefore, on consideration of 28%
including spine, the disability to the whole body after deduction of 1/3rd comes to 9.3% which is rounded off to 10%.
Accordingly, I deem it appropriate to take disability to the whole body at 10% as against 6% adopted by the tribunal.

Therefore, the loss of future earning capacity on the basis of income and disability is enhanced by this Court as follows:
Rs.1,94,400/- (Rs.9,000/- x 12 x 18 x 10%) as against Rs.77,760/- awarded by the tribunal.
14.
The tribunal has awarded Rs.17,373/- under the head of medical expenses, which is on the basis of actual bills produced by the claimant.
The same does not call for interference and it is retained.
15. The tribunal has awarded Rs.25,000/- under the heads of pain and suffering, which does not call for interference and same is retained.
16. With regard to compensation awarded under the head of attendant charges, nourishment and diet food, the - 11 - tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.

It is not clearly mentioned by the claimant as to how many days,
he was inpatient in the Hospital.
However, the tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/- under this head.
I do not find any illegality to interfere with the same.
Hence, the same is retained.
17. Under the head of loss of amenities, the tribunal has awarded Rs.10,000/-.
I am of the opinion that this is on the lower side for the reason that the claimant has undergone fracture and disability to an extent of 28% in all.
In view of the same, I deem it appropriate to award Rs.25,000/- under the head of loss of amenities as against Rs.10,000/- awarded by the tribunal.
18. Under the head of conveyance charges, the tribunal has awarded Rs.5,000/- which does not call for interference and same is retained.
19. It is seen that the tribunal has not awarded any amount under the head of loss of income during laid up period.

The claimant has undergone fracture to right pelvis and took treatment and also there being prolapse of IV disk and L-5 S01 and injury to spine and the medical evidence Devaraj K S vs Marulasiddeshwara R J on 31 March, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107752679/
5 - 12 - adduced by the Doctor-PW.2 also confirms that the claimant sustained 20% physical disability to the right lower limb and 8% to the spine which would evidence the fact that the claimant would have taken rest atleast for a period of three months for recuperation and get back to normal work.
